scope.slice_1: MIT retained render geometry with explicit assembly-body ownership, Arc-shared immutable f64 indexed meshes, physical cluster partition/remap and COM-frame shifts
scope.slice_2: GPL baker retains existing fuselage tessellator output in body-local frames with solved assembly poses and final COM translation; body_render controls offline sampling
scope.slice_3: wire v9 bounded on-change appearance, native heterogeneous opaque world draws at a bracketed PRIMARY presentation epoch, resolved disabled/quality policy
scope.not_implemented: full designs/assets/materials, wing/control-surface appearance, custom PRIMARY replacement, texture/PBR parity, incremental GPU source residency, prediction/reconciliation or complete Bevy replacement
scope.licensing: new mesh and instance-range contracts remain MIT; wire policy, baker and native game presentation remain GPL; no GPL source moved into engine crates

contracts.authority: render geometry never contributes mass/contact/aerodynamic/thermal forces; split ownership and recentering extend the existing reconstruction path, not a second physics system
contracts.mesh_validation: finite f64 vertices and part origins; unit normals/quaternions; in-range CCW triangle indices; assembly ownership required for assembled definitions and remapped on split; old JSON defaults empty
contracts.wire: v9 extends kind-10 FleetGeometry with RenderAppearance; absent/over-budget states explicit; v7/v8 rejected; existing revision and complete membership checks retained; no filenames, URLs, loader or full VehicleDefinition
contracts.catalogue_capacity: 63 secondaries, at most 64,512 admitted appearance vertices; existing 8 MiB frame cap; mesh bounds are checked after decoding and do not establish transient allocation safety
contracts.publication: source descriptors compare borrowed poses/labels and Arc identity before mesh values; vertex/index buffers are not deep-copied or encoded at snapshot cadence; the existing cached Arc frame and per-mailbox revision marker send only changes/new subscriptions
contracts.source_upload: native flattens static body-part transforms only on matched catalogue revision; combined source replacement reuploads PRIMARY too, and recreates the existing mesh pipeline/resources on the same device; empty catalogues do not copy/reupload PRIMARY; no incremental asset residency claim
contracts.steady_frame: existing renderer updates view, lighting and matrix buffers plus per-primitive instance ranges in one opaque pass; at most 64 matrices/4,672 frame-upload bytes including PRIMARY; admitted part ranges are filled linearly, not cross-product instance draws
contracts.common_epoch: available members retain two poses; inertial endpoint interpolation and f64 attitude slerp sample PRIMARY's scene epoch, followed by reference ephemeris subtraction at that epoch; exact samples work without history; geometry revisions reset tracks; no extrapolation or cross-clock substitution
contracts.freshness: observer rows keep own authoritative times; stale membership or mismatched geometry withholds world draws without inventing despawn; out-of-bracket objects expose epoch_withheld
contracts.quality: RequestedGraphics -> resolution -> renderer.fleet_meshes/fleet_min_pixels; Low/Medium/High choose estimated 8/2/0.5-pixel angular-footprint culling of identical mesh sources; near/intersecting bounds never size-cull; settings apply at renderer creation
contracts.disabled: no fleet GPU source/upload/draw or track history; original PRIMARY renderer remains; the independent contact inspector is still available
contracts.numeric_oracles: split world vertices <1 mm absolute at 3e12 m inertial distance; JSON coordinates within 1e-12 m for the fixture; static part-to-body narrowing checked <=1 mm before GPU allocation; moving-reference epoch interpolation oracle <1 mm and independent correct body axes
contracts.interpolation_limit: linear/slerp between observed endpoints, not a guaranteed trajectory error envelope or prediction/reconciliation; clocks outside the available interval withhold meshes
contracts.appearance: actual retained shells with explicitly neutral untextured finish, never a contact hull/X-15 substitution; PRIMARY remains the compatibility X-15

reproduction.replay_peer_source:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import pathlib, struct, sys, time
root = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
length = sys.stdin.buffer.read(4)
if len(length) != 4: raise SystemExit(1)
sys.stdin.buffer.read(struct.unpack('<I', length)[0])
sys.stdout.buffer.write((root / 'baked-render-separation.frame').read_bytes())
sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
samples = (root / 'baked-render-separation.samples').read_bytes()
while True:
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(samples)
    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
    time.sleep(0.05)

limitations: The current protocol is deliberately bounded to small retained body shells. Larger authored sources are omitted, not streamed incrementally or partially approximated.

Source changes rebuild/reupload the combined PRIMARY/fleet source on the existing device; static event cost and peak transient memory are not eliminated. There is no persistent incremental GPU asset registry.

A change to a part origin (including resource-driven COM recentering) revises the complete descriptor/catalogue even when mesh buffers are shared and unchanged. This may cause repeated network payloads and source uploads on an actively changing fleet; no incremental network mesh dictionary or production streaming-efficiency claim is made.

A secondary with simulation debt or insufficient history may remain invisible in the world until its interval covers PRIMARY's epoch; the own-time observer still reports it. No extrapolation hides this gap.
The frozen baked-assembly replay proves producer/physical split/wire/native consumption, not live separation-command acknowledgement or custom PRIMARY shape correctness.
The GPU oracle and capacity workload use synthetic poses/triangles and are not a physical fleet, full-size mesh fleet, terrain-depth beauty comparison or subjective preference review.

Neutral shells are not authored appearance/PBR/material parity. PRIMARY still uses X-15; wing/interior/mechanism appearance, full resources, prediction/reconciliation, terrain/topology/effects/platform gaps remain.

Local frame comparisons preserve a trajectory, not an identical asynchronous material-publication schedule or a proof of zero overhead. Remote CPU/GPU workloads run in wall time and cannot isolate HUD/network cost.
